title: Stochastic GPU Demand Sampler & Cost Allocation Workbook
body:
Purpose:
This workbook generates probabilistic hourly demand scenarios (Monte Carlo) for inference workloads and converts those scenarios into recommended GPU provisioning mixes and per-tenant cost allocations. Designed to feed Redwood Optimize scoring and to inform Dedicated/reserved sizing conversations.

High-level approach:
- Inputs tab accepts historical traffic summary (qps by hour, median tokens/request, batchability distribution, cold-start rates, KV cache hit rate) plus business parameters (SLO, penalty cost per missed request, reserved pricing vs preemptible/on-demand).
- Sampler tab runs N Monte Carlo trials for the planning window (typically 28 days but configurable). Each trial samples per-hour demand from fitted distributions and applies workload-level variability (burst probability, diurnal multiplier, weekday/weekend patterns).
- Pool-sim tab maps sampled demand into GPU-hour consumption via model throughput curves and batching efficiency functions. It also models warm vs cold sequence warmup cost and KV cache hit variance.
- Allocation tab performs per-tenant attribution using token-weighted share and a fairness adjustment for tenants with low batchability.
- Output tab summarizes percentile capacity requirements (P50/P75/P90/P95/P99), recommended reserved capacity commit to meet target percentile, and expected blended cost/unit.

Sheet descriptions and key cells (use these names to link downstream tooling):
- Inputs (sheet)
  - Inputs!B2: Planning window days (default 28)
  - Inputs!B3: Trials (Monte Carlo) (default 5,000)
  - Inputs!B5:B12: Historical hourly QPS summary (24 cells, mean)
  - Inputs!B14: Mean tokens per request
  - Inputs!B15: Tokens per request SD
  - Inputs!B17: Batchability distribution (0..1)
  - Inputs!B19: KV cache hit rate mean and sd
  - Inputs!B21: SLO latency ms and per-missed-request penalty $
  - Inputs!B23: Pricing: reserved $/GPU-hour, preemptible $/GPU-hour, on-demand $/GPU-hour

- Sampler (sheet)
  - Uses formula examples for Excel/Sheets: =NORM.INV(RAND(), mean, sd) for per-hour QPS sampling when distribution is approximately normal; fallback Poisson sampling for low counts: =POISSON.INV(RAND(), lambda)
  - Burst toggles: sample Bernoulli with p = burst_probability; when true multiply that hour's demand by burst_multiplier
  - Tokens sampled per request: =MAX(1, ROUND(NORM.INV(RAND(), Inputs!B14, Inputs!B15),0))

- Pool-sim (sheet)
  - Throughput curves (table): rows = model variant (e.g., 13B_fp16, 33B_q4_0), columns = seq_len/beam/batch_size -> tokens/sec per GPU.
  - Effective throughput per trial hour = LOOKUP(model_variant, seq_len)*batching_gain(batchability_sample)
  - GPU-hours required = (sampled_tokens_for_hour / tokens_per_gpu_hour) + warm_start_overhead_hours
  - Preemptible failure modeling: sample outage events with p per hour; if outage occurs, route load to fallback capacity and add penalty hours

- Allocation (sheet)
  - Per-tenant cost share = (tenant_tokens * tenant_batch_penalty_adj) / sum(all_tokens_adjusted) * total_cost_for_hour
  - Low-batchability uplift factor applied to tenants with batchability < 0.3 to account for higher per-token cost
  - Example formula: =IF(Batchability<0.3, TenantTokens * 1.25, TenantTokens)

- Outputs (sheet)
  - Aggregated percentiles across trials for GPU-hours/day and for peak-hour GPU count
  - Recommended reserved commit = P_target_percentile_peak * safety_factor (recommended safety_factor 1.05 - 1.15 depending on business tolerance)
  - Expected blended unit cost = (reserved_hours*reserved_rate + preempt_hours*preempt_rate + ondemand_hours*ondemand_rate) / total_tokens
  - Cost of missed-SLO events = Expected_missed_count * penalty

Key design choices and rationale (explicit so reviewers can tune knobs):
- Use Monte Carlo (5k+) to capture tail risk from correlated bursts across tenants rather than relying on simple peak multipliers. Correlated bursts drive the difference between P90 and P99 provisioning.
- Model batching explicitly as a distribution (batchability) instead of a single multiplier because tenant composition changes (small requests vs long-context). This makes per-tenant allocation more defensible.
- Mix reserved + preemptible + on-demand: reserved covers baseline steady-state at target percentile, preemptible picks up stochastic spikes at ~50-70% cheaper price but with outage modeling, on-demand for immediate failover.
- Include warm-start penalty: models with large KV/state have first-token overhead that reduces effective tokens/sec for first N seconds; important for conversational workloads with many short sessions.

How to use in practice:
1) Paste 28 days of hourly aggregate QPS into Inputs!B5:B676 (or link to a table).
2) Update pricing and model throughput table with the current benchmark numbers from Serving Runtime team.
3) Run sampling with trials >= 2,000 for quick sanity checks, >= 5,000 for final recommendations.
4) Review Outputs P95/P99. Use Allocation tab to produce per-customer cost estimates and to inform chargeback or SKU pricing adjustments.

Diagnostic plots and checks (suggested charts):
- Histogram of peak GPU-hours per trial (showing long tail)
- Time-series heatmap of P95 demand across the planning window (identify persistent daily peaks)
- Per-tenant cost breakout and contribution to tail events (who drives P99)

Limitations and follow-ups:
- Synthetic burst generation is heuristic; validate against historical incident windows and tune burst_probability and multiplier.
- Throughput curves must be refreshed whenever a new kernel/quantization option is introduced. Link to Serving Runtime benchmarks in linked_artifacts.
- Does not model multi-model packing optimization (packing across model families). Consider a follow-up sheet that includes a bin-packing approximation for mixed-model placement.

Notes (work-in-progress):
- TODO: add an "auto-fit" routine that guesses distribution families (log-normal vs normal vs Poisson) for each hour-of-day and selects sampling method automatically.
- TODO: wire outputs into Optimize API scoring endpoint: /optimize/v1/capacity-suggestion with JSON payload described in Confluence linked above.

Example quick sanity-check numbers (base run):
- Planning window 28d, trials 5k => P95 peak GPUs = 112, P99 peak GPUs = 165
- Recommended reserved commit (P95, safety 1.1) => 123 GPUs
- Blended unit cost (tokens per $1k) = 1.2M tokens per $1k (illustrative; update with real prices)

Revision history and authorship log:
- 2025-11-03 Maya T: initial draft workbook and sampling framework
- 2025-12-12 Luis R: added tenant allocation heuristic and low-batch uplift
- 2026-02-10 Anika B: tuned preemptible outage model and added warm-start penalty

If accepted, this workbook will be the canonical feeder for the Optimize "reserve suggestion" endpoint and for Dedicated sizing recommendations. Reviewers: please pay attention to the allocation fairness rule and to the choice of sampling distributions for low-traffic hours.
